posts.cooked:
Nothing from this contest will be published, made, or created by GtG. This is only for fun.

 

This week's event is a contest. Take a look at this picture:

 

![](upload://qtPSA2zxirFoRh076ZPMTLuGFre.jpeg)

 

This will be the picture for a new card in Legacy's deck. Your job is to create that card. You will need to provide the following information:

1) The title

2) The type

3) The full game text

4) The flavor text

GtG will be pick the winner based on how well the card feels and sounds like an SotM card, and how well it fits into Legacy's deck.

In addition to bragging rights, the winner will get to have a 10 minute Google Hangout with the GtG team. This will happen in early December, and the winner will be notified on how to set it up.

Please keep all discussions about this event in this thread, and post all submissions into this thread.

 

Results due by Monday, November 18, 8:00 AM CST.

 

Nothing from this contest will be published, made, or created by GtG. This is only for fun.

posts.name: Benhimself
posts.cooked:
A simple but kind of mindbending idea I had which I didn't go with:

 

COHESIVE UNIT (Ongoing, limited)

H is reduced by 1.

 

It's a little game-breaking in certain situations, but so are quite a few other cards (next evolution versus certain opponents, say, or twist the ether versus single-source villains when teamed with Ra or AZ). It's a solid enough card that it's probably worth a drawback if I were to fully flesh out the idea, but I just dig how the mechanic fits into the theme: that of Legacy leading them as a well-knit team who can work more closely together than another team with similar numbers.

 

(Maybe something like: "If a hero ongoing would be destroyed by anything other than itself, destroy Cohesive Unit instead" or something, so it's more vulnerable to ongoing destruction? Or just "At the start of Legacy's turn, you must either skip your play phase, skip your power phase, or destroy this card." to represent his effort coordinating the battle.)

posts.name: Benhimself
posts.cooked:
Well, discussing mechanics is probably good practice for imaginary designers, so let's look at it this way.

 

In cases where you're being dealt H-based damage, Cohesive Unit will block one of that damage. Some times, yes, that'll be going from 1 to 0, but that's not exactly unheard of. Cohesive Unit can totally block the Matriach's H-2 retaliation damage when H=3, but so can Twist the Ether, or that one vat in Pike Industrial Complex, or any of the cards like Fortitude when the hero in question is the one with the highest HP. I mean, Legacy alone, whose deck it would be going in, has at least 3 ways he could block the Matriach's retaliation damage at H=3 (Fortidue while being the highest, heroic intervention while not being the highest, or lead from the front and next evolution at any time, which would also work at any H too). So, blocking one damage: not exactly game breaking, right?

 

Other times, Cohesive Unit might save a person from taking damage (if an effect hits H-1 or H-2 targets), or stop a card from being played (if an effect looks for H cards of a specific type), or possibly being played (if an effect looks at the top H cards of the villain deck and plays all of a specific type), or stop an ongoing or equipment from being destroyed (yada yada). These are all handy! But there's just as many times when it won't do anything at all: there's plenty of bad guy plays that don't involve H at all, and you might be sitting there wishing you had spent your turn playing a Heroic Intervention or Take Down instead, even if those just last for a single round.

 

Which, leading things back to more general hypothetical-designer talk if I may, is a good thing. It's important (at least in my humble opinion) for new cards to create new and interesting choices: something that's always better than an existing option in every situation  or good enough in general that it's an obvious must-play the second you draw it, removes choices, instead.

posts.name: phantaskippy
posts.cooked:
I think the card could work well if there was a cost.  Having it just an ongoing makes it potentially too powerful as there is no maintenance cost.

Discarding a card each round to keep it out, or even a rule 15 damage clause would balance it.  Fortitude needs Legacy to be highest HP or lead from the front to work, and then only vs. villains.  Next Evolution costs a power each round, and again lead from the front or Legacy being the only one targetted.

(H)-1 gives a lot of benefit to the whole team, and it requires no other cards to work well, and as written no cost to keep the effect.

I would go with the discard each round, or maybe a clause that if the villain does not deal damage for an entire round the card is destroyed.

 

As for the contest, do we have any idea when the winner will be announced?
